s0DDD2E.name: Objects: solid edges, solid dirt, steep slope dispatch
summary: Three extended-object routines. All write Map16 tile numbers into the level buffer: [$6B] is the low-byte plane ($7E:C800) and
[$6E] the high-byte (page) plane ($7F:C800); Sta1To6ePointer / StzTo6ePointer set the page to 1 / 0 before each store.
$0DDD2E: solid edges with bottoms. [$59] low nibble = type 0-3, high nibble = number of upper tiles; ends with a bottom tile.
$0DDD5C: solid dirt, a block of tile $165, width [$59] & $0F + 1 and height ([$59] >> 4) + 1.
$0DDD87: very steep slopes, picks left or right by bit 4 of [$59]. Parameters: [$57]: start position, [$59]: size/type.

PtrsLong0DDD93.name: Very steep slopes: left and right
summary: Two 3-byte pointers (left, right) followed by their routines. Each draws one column at a time with a top tile, a middle tile,
a bottom tile and then dirt fill below ($03F), starting two rows lower and one column over each time (columns 2 tiles shorter).
Slope tiles: left $1CA/$1CB/$1F1, right $1CC/$1CD/$1F2. Parameters: [$57]: start position, [$59] & $0F: width.

s0DDEDC.name: Canvass tile rows and screen pointers (7E)
summary: Tile rows for the 8 hard-coded canvasses, their positions in screen 0, and the 16 per-screen pointers into the $7E:C800 Map16
low-byte buffer (each screen is $01B0 bytes, 16 x 27 tiles).

s0DDF1A.name: Screen pointers into the 7F Map16 buffer
summary: Same 16 screen pointers as above for the $7F high-byte buffer.

s0DDF3A.name: Object: multiple canvasses (hardcoded position)
summary: Draws the canvass strip layout of screen 0 (five rows of tile $161 and 8 canvasses at fixed positions from the tables above),
then copies screen 0's low and high Map16 bytes to screens 1..[$59] with MVN. Parameters: [$59] & $0F: number of screens to fill.

s0DE05E.name: Table: canvass 1-4 tile layouts
summary: Four layouts of 19 bytes each: top row of 4 tiles (page 1), four middle rows of 3 tiles (page 0), last row of 3 tiles of $076.
The $60 in the top row is drawn as tile $160.

s0DE0AE.name: Object: canvass 1-4
summary: Draws one 4-wide, 6-row canvass from the tables above; the extended object number $71-$74 selects the layout.
Parameters: [$57]: position, [$59]: object number.

s0DE12C.name: Table: four-sided ground square tiles
summary: 3 rows (top, middle, bottom) of left, middle and right tiles, page 1.

s0DE135.name: Object: four-sided edge ground square
summary: Rectangle with a left, middle and right tile per row and separate top, middle and bottom row tiles.
Parameters: [$57]: position, [$59] & $0F: width, [$59] >> 4: height (rows = height + 1).

s0DE186.name: Freespace, then tileset Map16 definitions ($0DE300)
summary: $0DE186-$0DE2FF is $FF padding. From $0DE300 the data is a tileset-specific block of Map16 definitions, 8 bytes per tile:
four (8x8 character, property) pairs in the order top-left, bottom-left, top-right, bottom-right (checked: e.g. at $0DE428 the
second pair is the first one's lower half and the last two are the X-flipped copies). Property is YXPCCCTT.
This block is selected by tilesets 4, 5 and $0D in TilesetMAP16Loc ($05:8000). Row numbers #nn are the position in the block;
the Map16 number depends on the loader's bit mask at $05:81BB so it is not derived here.

s0DE890.name: Dispatch: objects for tileset 4 (ghost house)
summary: Calls the routine for object [$5A] through ExecutePtrLong using the table below (object 1 = first entry).
Used when the tileset is T:4 in Lunar Magic (ghost house or switch palace).

PtrsLong0DE921.name: Object $2E pointer: Thin horizontal upward spikes

PtrsLong0DE933.name: Object $34 pointer: Wood ledge on column

PtrsLong0DE93C.name: Object $37 pointer: Horizontal log background and hand rails

PtrsLong0DE93F.name: Object $38 pointer: Wood ledge without column

PtrsLong0DE942.name: Object $39 pointer: Some vertical log backgrounds

PtrsLong0DE945.name: Object $3A pointer: Solid vertical brick edges and spikes

PtrsLong0DE948.name: Object $3B pointer: Wood thingy ledge (bonus rooms)

PtrsLong0DE94B.name: Object $3C pointer: Upside down ledge (switch palace)

PtrsLong0DE951.name: Object $3E pointer: Right facing edge (switch palace)

PtrsLong0DE954.name: Object $3F pointer, corner tiles, large background
summary: $0DE954: pointer to the left facing switch palace edge routine (CODE_0DEE89).
$0DE957: tiles for the switch palace corners ($073-$076) and brick background bits ($093-$096).
$0DE95F: writes one tile from that table; index = [$59] - $57 (extended objects $57-$5E). Parameters: [$57]: position.
$0DE971: large background area, fills 4 x 256 tiles of $077 (page 0) starting at the current pointer [$6B].

s0DE98F.name: Table: ghost house clock and beam 1 tiles
summary: Three 3x3 pieces, 9 bytes each: clock, beam top-left to bottom-right, beam top-right to bottom-left. Tile $025 is empty background.

s0DE9AA.name: Object: ghost house clock and beams (3x3)
summary: Draws a 3x3 piece from the table above. Parameters: [$57]: position, [$59]: extended object $61-$63.

s0DE9E1.name: Table: ghost house cobweb and window tiles
summary: 2x2 tiles each: cobweb top right, cobweb top left, window.

s0DE9ED.name: Object: ghost house cobwebs and window (2x2)
summary: Draws a 2x2 piece. Cobwebs are extended objects $64-$65; the window routine (CODE_0DECC1) jumps in at $0DE9F5 with X = 8.

s0DEA1E.name: Table: ghost house beam 2 tiles
summary: Two 4x4 pieces (16 bytes each): beam top-right to bottom-left, top-left to bottom-right.

s0DEA3E.name: Object: ghost house beams (4x4)
summary: Draws a 4x4 piece. Parameters: [$57]: position, [$59]: extended object $66-$67.

s0DEA71.name: Table: ghost house exit tiles
summary: 13 rows of 6 tiles (page 0).

s0DEABF.name: Object: ghost house exit (6x13)
summary: Draws the exit tiles from DATA_0DEA71. Parameters: [$57]: position.

s0DEADE.name: Table: ghost house entrance tiles
summary: 14 rows of 10 tiles (page 0).

s0DEB6A.name: Object: ghost house entrance (10x14)
summary: Draws the entrance tiles from DATA_0DEADE. Parameters: [$57]: position.

s0DEB93.name: Table: Yoshi's house tiles
summary: 10 rows of 16 tiles, used by the Yoshi's house object that follows this chunk.
